text:
alex: Customer (FintechX) reports intermittent stalled SSE streams after token refresh. They see partial output, then connection closes without final "done" event. Happened ~10% of requests. Escalating — customer on Dedicated.
maria: Any correlation with auth rotate? They said token rotated at ~30s into session.
jordan: Can you paste a sample trace? Also what SDK + version?
alex: Using py-sdk v0.9.4. Added logs: server sends final frame but client doesn't turn final chunk into message, iterator hangs. log excerpt:
```
[server] 2026-03-14T10:12:32Z send: data: {"id":"chunk-12","delta":"..."}
[server] 2026-03-14T10:12:32Z send: data: {"event":"done"}
[edge] 2026-03-14T10:12:32Z 101 Switching Protocols
[proxy] 2026-03-14T10:12:32Z auth: refresh start
[client] 2026-03-14T10:12:32Z recv: partial bytes then EOF
```
elaine: Interesting — proxy does auth refresh right around the final frame. Could be that chunk boundary and auth handshake cause the connection to be torn down mid-chunk.
maria: Does the py-sdk buffer by newline or by parsing full SSE events? If it's streaming parser that waits for double newline it could block on partial final event.
jordan: I dug into iterator: py-sdk uses a readline-like loop over bytes and yields when it sees a blank line. If connection closed without CRLFCRLF it can hang until recv returns 0, but we saw EOF.
alex: The customer's client never receives the "event: done" SSE event in their app, but server log shows it sent. Proxy trace shows a 401 -> token rotate -> 200 re-establish. Possibly two back-to-back socket closes cause OS to drop last packet.
elaine: Quick repro steps I gave them:
- run local proxy that simulates token rotate at 30s
- use our python iterator sample
- capture tcpdump on client
They reproduced locally with our script.
maria: Can we get tcpdump / pcap? We need to know if final packet left server. If it left and didn't arrive, routing issue. If not, server closed early.
jordan: Customer attached pcap; I reviewed — final "done" packet was sent, ACKed by proxy, then OS sent FIN from proxy to client during auth handoff, client saw FIN before reading remaining buffer due to half-close handling in python socket recv.
alex: So client recv got zero-length? That explains iterator hang — our iterator expects newline delimiting but when socket returns 0 bytes we do break loop but last buffered partial event isn't emitted.
elaine: Proposed fix: on socket close, flush buffer as a final event if non-empty. That would yield partial message and then raise StopAsyncIteration. Also add a short application-level heartbeat to guarantee final newline.
jordan: I can whip up a small patch for py-sdk: after recv==b'' check buffer != '' -> yield buffer as final chunk. Add unit test simulating EOF mid-event.
maria: Also add a mitigation doc for customers: set keepalive/tcp_fin_timeout and recommend token rotation windows that avoid mid-request rotate. For Dedicated, suggest rotating tokens out-of-band or using session-scoped tokens.
alex: Escalating to eng-runtime to confirm whether we can make proxy auth handoff less disruptive. Filed INT-4289 and attached pcap + repro. Tagging @eng-runtime.
eng-runtime-bot: New issue INT-4289 created by alex: "SSE final-frame lost during proxy auth handoff". Priority: P2. Assigned to jordan.
jordan: I'll land py-sdk patch today and tag a canary build. Also will add logging to console to surface when EOF occurs with non-empty buffer.
elaine: Customer-facing response drafted: apologize, explain root cause (proxy FIN during auth rotation can drop last buffered SSE frame at client), provide workaround (upgrade py-sdk to patch x.y.z, enable heartbeat, adjust token rotation timing). Send once canary verified.
alex: Customer accepted workaround and will test canary tomorrow. For tracking: support ticket 78932. Closing with follow-up in 48h.
